result.reason: B is clearer and better matched to the client. On clarity: B sequences the quarter logically, keeps sentences short, and frames the fee change unambiguously as a benefit ("works in your favor," "existing rates are unchanged"), whereas A says fees "will be adjusted" and leaves the client to work out whether they are better or worse off. A also contains a parsing stumble ("declined by -2.95%") and muddles whether the 0.5% figure covers the month or the quarter. B additionally gives year-to-date and trailing-twelve-month context so the reader can size a down quarter without doing the work themselves. On tone: the notes call for a direct, non-defensive answer to Samuel's question about whether the screen costs money. B names him and answers immediately ("This quarter, it did"), quantifies the cost, and declines to talk around it, then balances with what the screen delivered. A defends unprompted ("rather than a failure of management"), hedges before answering, buries the response without naming Samuel, and uses marketing language ("ensuring that leadership ... aligns with long-term sustainability goals") that a skeptic will read as spin. Preference is not length-driven; the letters are comparable in length and B is tighter per point. Minor suggested edits to B: add a lead-in to the verbatim disclosure and reduce the bolding.
